postTitle: Gig and Informal Work: Planning Without an Employer
topic: A freelance day rate has to fund everything an employer paid for

assumptions.notes: Salaried job €40,000 a year, about 260 working days, all paid: €40,000 ÷ 260 = about €154 a paid day. Employer adds a 5% pension contribution (€2,000) and sick pay and insurance. Freelancer: 260 days less 25 holiday, 10 public holidays and 5 sick days = 220; about a fifth unbilled leaves about 176 billable days. Needs €40,000 + €2,000 pension + roughly €2,000 insurance = €44,000. €44,000 ÷ 176 = €250 a day, about 1.6 times €154. Charging €154 is a pay cut of more than a third (154 ÷ 250 = 0.62). Common rule of thumb: 1.5 to 2 times. Illustrative.

caption.instagram:
Freelancing at your old salary's day rate? For the same life, that is a pay cut.

A €40,000 salary is paid over about 260 days, about €154 each, with a pension contribution and sick pay on top. A freelancer is paid only for days billed: take out holidays, public holidays and sick days, then a fifth for finding work and invoicing, and about 176 days are left. Replacing the salary, a €2,000 pension contribution and roughly €2,000 of insurance takes €44,000, or €250 a billable day, about 1.6 times. Charging €154 is a pay cut of more than a third.

Price your bundle: working days less leave, less unbilled time; salary plus pension and insurance; divide one by the other.
